name: owasp-benchmark
notes: UNVERIFIED in this build environment (no network here to build/pull images or fetch the CSV) — the operator must verify against a live instance. Ground truth is OWASP's OWN published expectedresults-1.2.csv (neutral, independently authored — NOT our curation); set ground_truth.owasp_csv to that file's path (relative to the corpus base_dir, or absolute). dast_only=true restricts scoring to the honest black-box-reachable categories (cmdi, sqli, xss, pathtraver, ldapi, xpathi); the SAST-only categories (crypto, hash, securecookie, trustbound, weakrand) are intentionally excluded from recall — score those with a SAST tool. Locations resolve to /benchmark/<test name> (e.g. /benchmark/BenchmarkTest00001), matching the ~2,740 endpoints CRUCIBLE crawls from the seed. Canonical source: there is NO official Docker Hub image; OWASP Benchmark 1.2 is built from source (github.com/OWASP-Benchmark/BenchmarkJava, project home owasp.org/www-project-benchmark) — the image tag 'owasp-benchmark:1.2' is a LOCALLY-BUILT placeholder the operator produces (runBenchmark.sh compiles the Java suite and serves it under Tomcat). Default deployment is HTTPS with a self-signed cert on 8443 (container_port set to that canonical default); note that the harness's built-in DockerLauncher health check and scanner speak plain HTTP, so the operator must EITHER enable Tomcat's plain-HTTP connector on 8080 and change container_port to 8080, OR supply an HTTPS-aware launcher pointing at the running instance. heavy=true: this is a RAM/CPU-heavy Java/Tomcat build that is never auto-launched — run_corpus_app refuses to launch it without an operator-provided launcher. No login is required (test pages are unauthenticated) and the suite is self-contained (embedded DB, server-rendered JSP — no external database or SPA to stand up), but each test case consumes its input via a specific vector — query string, POST form body, cookie, or header — hence the broad insertion_kinds; some cases only trigger on POST bodies. max_audit_requests=0 means UNCAPPED audit traffic (0 is the no-budget-limit sentinel, not zero requests), which is what a full recall pass needs. Timing checks are dropped (drop_timing=true) because per-endpoint timing probes across ~2,740 endpoints are infeasibly slow; the DAST-reachable categories are confirmable without them (time-based SQLi still credits the sqli label via boolean/error-based detections under the family class-key). max_pages=150 will not cover all ~2,740 endpoints in one pass — raise it (and max_depth) for fuller recall at the cost of runtime.
